properties.areaDesc: Coastal Colleton; Charleston
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 25 at 2:35PM EDT until October 25 at 10:00PM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 6 feet
in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one half
foot of inundation above ground level expected along shorelines
and tidal waterways (7.2 to 7.4 feet Mean Lower Low Water at
Charleston). For the Coastal Flood Watch, one to two feet of
inundation above ground level possible along shorelines and
tidal waterways (7.9 to 8.1 feet Mean Lower Low Water at
Charleston).

* WHERE...Coastal Colleton and Charleston Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Monday evening.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 5 PM EDT Monday. For the
Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 PM EDT this evening. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, from late tonight through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Significant saltwater inundation will render
numerous roads impassable. Properties may also flood.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tide will occur around 7:56 PM today
and 8:18 AM Monday at Charleston. Saltwater inundation will be
possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide. Beach erosion
is most likely to occur near the time of high tides.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Visit water.weather.gov for additional water level and flood
impact information.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

Weather Radio broadcasts.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Moderate coastal flooding around periods of high tide,
reaching major flood stage on Monday and Tuesday. Life
threatening rip currents are expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Broward County and Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 AM EDT Monday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 2 AM Monday to 8 PM EDT
Tuesday. Coastal Flood Advisories will then be necessary through
much of next week after the peak of King Tides. For the High
Rip Current Risk, through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor to moderate coastal flooding expected due to very
high tides.

* WHERE...Coastal areas of Los Angeles, Ventura, Santa Barbara,
and San Luis Obispo Counties.

* WHEN...From 5 AM Sunday to 1 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike
paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach
erosion is likely. Isolated damage of structures due to sea
water inundation is possible to the most vulnerable areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will likely reach 7.5-8.0 feet
(MLLW) each late morning, which is 1.0 to 1.5 feet above
astronomical projections. The highest tides will be Monday
through Wednesday. There is a small chance for isolated Coastal
Flood Warnings Wednesday through Thursday if larger surf
develops.

barricades or through water of unknown depth.
